queue.dek: Gavin Newsom spared 548 California death row inmates on Nov. 5. He waited till he had one foot out the door.
queue.opening: Not all murders are eligible for the death penalty. In fact, murder alone is almost never sufficient for society’s ultimate punishment. It must be murder plus what we call an aggravating circumstance, such as the murder of more than one person, the murder of a child or a murder in the commission of another crime, such as burglary, rape or robbery. In the universe of capital-eligible cases, very few death sentences are sought and even fewer are given. For those given, the process is rightfully arduous. The prosecution must convince the jury of both the underlying crimes and that death is the proper sentence. Those are separate trials. In other words, 12 people must agree, beyond a reasonable doubt, twice before anyone can be sentenced to death. And the return of the death verdict is only the beginning of the appellate process. There are direct appeals , collateral appeals and challenges to everything the police, prosecutors, defense attorneys and judges do and say. And even though I handled seven death penalty cases to verdict, I full well understand those who are opposed to capital punishment and have spent no time trying to change their minds. To serve on a death penalty jury, each potential juror is questioned individually about his or her beliefs, background and understanding of the law. queue.dek: Minnesota farmer Shayne Isane says gray wolves killed three calves in one night, costing thousands as Trump moves to reconsider federal protections.
queue.opening: A powerful apex predator has reignited a fierce battle between farmers demanding greater control over gray wolves killing their livestock and environmentalists fighting to keep them shielded — a decision the Trump administration must now weigh that could shape the future of wildlife management. One longtime Minnesota farmer has spent years grappling with the loss of several of his calves killed by gray wolves, also known as timber wolves, roaming around his property in the middle of the night. "We can walk right outside of our door and hear the howling of these timber wolves, and it'll send shivers down your spine because you have seen what they can do, and they're the top-of-the-line predator," Shayne Isane told Fox News Digital. "There's nothing that hunts them. No other animals they are afraid of." ARCTIC WOLF ATTACKS CHILD DURING ZOOKEEPER EVENT, GIRL AIRLIFTED TO HOSPITAL Isane, who has farmed for nearly four decades, said he is one of many farmers struggling to defend his livestock from gray wolves . Despite losing thousands of dollars and fearing for the safety of his nearly 300 cattle, Isane said he is unable to handle the threat himself. "Even if we see them attacking our livestock, we can't shoot or try to help out our animals," he said. "It's just against the law. We can't do it, only in the case of the threat of human life, which is a tough sell for us, because when you see them very close to your livelihood, your families and your livestock, it's a huge concern."

"I would do it," Trump responded. "These credit card companies have made a lot and the credit card fees that they charge, I'm all into it." Trump acknowledged that some critics could view the proposed cap as inconsistent with free-market principles, but argued that consumers should not face excessive fees.
